overview: Psychometry is a adept-level light side technique classified under Sense. Reads the history and emotional residue imprinted on objects through touch, revealing past events as vivid sensory flashes. Quinlan Vos was renowned for psychometric tracking, using a mere fragment of cloth to locate abducted targets across the galaxy.
history:
Force scholars trace Psychometry across eras recorded in holocrons, Jedi Archives data-tapes, and Sith tombs on Korriban and Dromund Kaas. Practitioners documented in Clone Wars · High Republic · Dark Disciple · KOTOR II established the modern understanding of how this ability manifests in combat, meditation, and ritual.

During the Old Republic and Sith Empire conflicts, masters drilled Psychometry into initiates as part of the standard curriculum for sense specialisation. Surviving battle logs from the Clone Wars and Galactic Civil War show the technique adapted to blaster-era warfare, starfighter engagements, and close-quarters lightsaber duels.

In the sequel era, surviving texts and oral traditions kept knowledge of Psychometry alive even as the Jedi Temple fell and the Sith assumed new forms. Each generation reinterpreted the power through its own doctrine while the underlying Force mechanism — channelled midi-chlorian symbiosis and focused will — remained constant.

The Jedi teach that this ability must serve life, consent, and the greater good — never domination or fear.
significance:
Psychometry exemplifies how sense abilities shape Force doctrine on the light side. At adept mastery, users balance raw potential against discipline, emotional control, and the moral weight of their choices.

Historians note that armies and orders rose or fell partly on how widely and wisely this technique was taught. A single master of Psychometry could turn a skirmish, break a siege, or unravel an enemy's will before blades crossed.

For students today — in academies, hidden enclaves, or alone with ancient texts — Psychometry remains a benchmark of sense proficiency across the Star Wars saga.
